<reason>A won by making the motion’s own standard—long-term debris cascades—the deciding test and showing that “all” does not follow from it. Known high vs. low intercepts, independent observation of decay, and the incentive point that a blanket ban deletes the clean path while leaving China/Russia as unenforceable as before, outlasted B’s prestige and bright-line replies. B stayed coherent on not unspreading a cloud, but had to recast months of transient crossing risk as cascade onset, which A used to collapse the justification. A’s clipped close is a real cost, not enough to flip a clearer comparative case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Q2 plus Rebuttal 2: B could not name lasting cascade harm from 2008/2019 and shifted to a collision lottery; A showed that swap abandoned the motion and that a ceiling preserves responsible testing B’s “all” would erase.</best_rebuttal>
